Title: Diagnosis
Details:
- What the test does
  - testWriteNonAsciiDirectoryNamePosixMode creates a directory entry with a non‑ASCII name "föö/" and enables writing of POSIX/PAX headers for non‑ASCII names, then calls TarArchiveOutputStream.putArchiveEntry on it.

- How putArchiveEntry triggers PAX header writing
  - In TarArchiveOutputStream.putArchiveEntry:
    - It prepares a map of PAX headers.
    - Since addPaxHeadersForNonAsciiNames is true and the entry name contains non‑ASCII characters, it adds a "path" PAX header for the entry name (lines 302–305).
    - Because there are headers to write, it calls writePaxHeaders(entryName, paxHeaders) (lines 313–315).

- How the PAX header entry is constructed incorrectly
  - In writePaxHeaders:
    - It builds a name for the PAX header entry as "./PaxHeaders.X/" + stripTo7Bits(entryName) (line 456).
    - If that resulting name is >= 100 characters, it truncates it to 99 characters (lines 459–461) with a comment noting: “TarEntry's constructor would think this is a directory and not allow any data to be written” (lines 457–461).
    - It constructs a TarArchiveEntry for the PAX header with that name and type LF_PAX_EXTENDED_HEADER_LC (lines 462–464).
    - It then writes the computed PAX key=value data into this entry (lines 486–491).

- Why the PAX header entry is treated as a directory
  - TarArchiveEntry(String name) sets directory-related fields based on whether the name ends with "/" (lines 224–235); TarArchiveEntry(String, byte) then overrides the linkFlag but does not change the name (lines 250–257).
  - Because the original entry was a directory ("föö/"), the PAX header name built by "./PaxHeaders.X/" + stripTo7Bits(entryName) also ends with a trailing "/".
  - This makes the TarArchiveEntry constructed for the PAX header look like a directory based on its name. Even though the linkFlag is later set to the PAX header type, checks like isDirectory likely still evaluate true due to the trailing slash in the name.

- How this leads to the exception
  - Back in TarArchiveOutputStream.putArchiveEntry for the PAX entry:
    - It sets currSize to 0 if entry.isDirectory() is true; otherwise to entry.getSize() (lines 323–327). Because the PAX entry name ends with "/", entry.isDirectory() is treated as true and currSize is set to 0.
  - writePaxHeaders then writes the PAX data bytes (line 489). The write method enforces that the number of written bytes must not exceed currSize:
    - TarArchiveOutputStream.write throws an IOException if currBytes + numToWrite > currSize (lines 386–391).
    - Since currSize is 0 and PAX data length is > 0, the exception “request to write '…' bytes exceeds size in header of '0' bytes for entry './PaxHeaders.X/…/'” is thrown.

- Why this matches both the test failure and the issue report
  - The test uses a non‑ASCII directory name and enables PAX headers, leading to the PAX pseudo‑entry being misclassified as a directory due to a trailing slash, causing the exact size‑mismatch exception when writing PAX data.
  - The issue report describes the same exception when storing long directory names: the constructed PAX header entry name ends with “/”, making it look like a directory with size 0. The attempted workaround in writePaxHeaders (truncating if length >= 100) is not robust—short names (like in the test) aren’t truncated and still end with “/”; even for long names, truncation may still leave a trailing “/”.

Root cause:
- writePaxHeaders uses the original entry name (which ends with “/” for directories) to build the PAX header entry name, so the PAX header entry is treated as a directory. This results in currSize being set to 0 for the PAX entry and subsequent attempts to write the PAX data failing with an IOException.

Evidence:
- TarArchiveOutputStream.putArchiveEntry: lines 302–315, 317–327.
- TarArchiveOutputStream.writePaxHeaders: lines 456–491.
- TarArchiveEntry constructors: lines 224–242, 250–257.
- TarArchiveOutputStream.write: lines 386–391.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
